name: Arianism
condemned_by: Condemned at the Council of Nicaea (325) and Constantinople (381)
teaches: Jesus is a created being, a first and greatest creature, not eternally God.
markers: there was a time when the Son was not
Jesus was created by the Father
Christ is a lesser god or a created being
the Son is not of the same essence as the Father
orthodox: The Son is eternally God, of one being with the Father (Nicene Creed).

name: Nestorianism
condemned_by: Condemned at the Council of Ephesus (431)
teaches: Christ is two separate persons, one divine and one human, joined only morally; Mary bore only the human Jesus, not God.
markers: Mary is not the mother of God
the divine Christ and the human Jesus are two persons
the Word merely dwelt in the man Jesus like a temple
orthodox: Christ is one person in two natures; Mary is rightly called Theotokos, bearer of God (Ephesus 431).

name: Eutychianism (Monophysitism)
condemned_by: Condemned at the Council of Chalcedon (451)
teaches: Christ's humanity was absorbed into or mixed with his divinity, so he had only one blended nature.
markers: Christ had only one nature, the divine
his humanity was swallowed up by his deity
Jesus was not truly human in the same way we are
orthodox: Christ has two natures, fully God and fully man, without confusion or change (Chalcedon 451). Note: some Oriental Orthodox churches confess one united nature (miaphysitism) and reject this label.

name: Docetism
condemned_by: Rejected in the New Testament (1 John 4:2-3) and by the early church
teaches: Jesus only appeared to be human and to suffer; his body was an illusion or a phantom.
markers: Jesus only seemed to have a body
Christ did not really suffer or die on the cross
the divine Christ left Jesus before the crucifixion
orthodox: The Word became flesh (John 1:14); Jesus truly lived, suffered, died and rose in a real body.

name: Modalism (Sabellianism)
condemned_by: Condemned in the 3rd century (Sabellius excommunicated c. 220) and rejected in the Nicene Creed
teaches: God is one person who appears in three modes or masks (Father, Son, Spirit) at different times, rather than three persons at once.
markers: God is one person who shows up as Father, then Son, then Spirit
the Father himself died on the cross
Father, Son and Spirit are just three names or roles for the same person
orthodox: One God eternally in three distinct persons, Father, Son and Holy Spirit.

name: Adoptionism
condemned_by: Condemned at the Synod of Antioch (268) with Paul of Samosata, and in later councils
teaches: Jesus was an ordinary man whom God adopted as Son at his baptism or resurrection; he was not eternally the Son.
markers: Jesus became God's Son at his baptism
God promoted a good man to divine sonship
Jesus earned his divinity by his obedience
orthodox: The Son is eternally God and became man in the incarnation.

name: Apollinarianism
condemned_by: Condemned at the Council of Constantinople (381)
teaches: Christ had a human body but the divine Word took the place of a human mind or soul.
markers: Christ had no human mind or soul
the Logos replaced Jesus's human spirit
orthodox: Christ assumed a complete human nature: body, soul and mind.

name: Monothelitism
condemned_by: Condemned at the Third Council of Constantinople (681)
teaches: Christ had only one will, the divine, with no distinct human will.
markers: Christ had only a divine will
Jesus had no human will of his own
orthodox: Christ has a divine will and a human will, the human freely submitting to the divine (Gethsemane).

name: Tritheism
condemned_by: Rejected in the Nicene and Athanasian creeds
teaches: Father, Son and Spirit are three separate gods, not one God.
markers: there are three gods
Father, Son and Spirit are three separate beings who cooperate like a committee
orthodox: There is one God in three persons, one divine essence.

name: Socinianism and Unitarianism
condemned_by: Rejected by Reformation confessions and the historic creeds
teaches: Denies the Trinity and the deity of Christ; Jesus was a mere man (sometimes divinely favored) and the Spirit is a force, not a person.
markers: Jesus was only a man and not God
the Holy Spirit is just a force or power, not a person
the Trinity is a pagan invention
orthodox: Jesus is God incarnate and the Holy Spirit is a divine person (Nicene Creed).

name: Ebionism
condemned_by: Rejected by the early church fathers
teaches: Jesus was a merely human Messiah, and Gentile believers must keep the Jewish law to be saved.
markers: Jesus was a mere man chosen as Messiah
you must keep the Law of Moses to be saved
Paul corrupted the gospel
orthodox: Jesus is fully God and fully man; salvation is by grace through faith, not by the works of the law (Galatians, Acts 15).

name: Pelagianism
condemned_by: Condemned at the Councils of Carthage (418) and Ephesus (431)
teaches: People are born morally unharmed and can obey God and earn salvation by their own effort without grace; there is no inherited sin.
markers: we are born without sin
we can earn our salvation by good works
we can obey God perfectly by willpower alone
original sin does not exist
God's favor is a reward for how good we are
orthodox: All are fallen in Adam and are saved by grace alone through faith, which also empowers obedience (Eph 2:8-9; Rom 5).

name: Gnosticism
condemned_by: Refuted by Irenaeus and rejected by the early church
teaches: Salvation comes through secret knowledge; matter and the body are evil; the creator God of the Old Testament is a lesser or evil being.
markers: salvation comes through secret knowledge
the physical world and our bodies are evil prisons
the God of the Old Testament is a different, lesser god
only the spiritually enlightened can understand the real gospel
orthodox: Creation is good; salvation is by faith in the crucified and risen Christ, open to all, not by hidden knowledge.

name: Marcionism
condemned_by: Marcion excommunicated at Rome (c. 144)
teaches: Rejects the Old Testament and its God as inferior or different from the Father of Jesus; keeps only an edited New Testament.
markers: the God of the Old Testament is not the Father of Jesus
we should throw out the Old Testament
the Old Testament God is angry and Jesus's God is loving, so they are different gods
orthodox: The God of Israel is the Father of Jesus Christ; the whole Bible is one story.

name: Manichaeism
condemned_by: Condemned by the early church (refuted by Augustine) and the Roman Empire
teaches: Cosmic dualism: eternal equal forces of good (spirit, light) and evil (matter, darkness) at war.
markers: evil is an eternal power equal to God
the material world was made by the dark power
the soul is a spark of light trapped in a body
orthodox: God alone is eternal and good; evil is a corruption of creation, not an equal power.

name: Montanism
condemned_by: Rejected by synods in Asia Minor and by the early church
teaches: New prophecy supersedes or equals Scripture; ecstatic prophets are the final authority.
markers: new revelation from our prophet replaces the Bible
the Spirit is giving us a message that goes beyond and overrides Scripture
only our prophet speaks the final word of God
orthodox: Scripture is the final, sufficient rule; any prophecy is tested by it (1 Thess 5:20-21). Note: simply believing prophecy continues today is not Montanism.

name: Donatism
condemned_by: Condemned at the Councils of Arles (314) and Carthage (411)
teaches: Sacraments and ministry are invalid if the minister is sinful or unworthy; the church must be pure of sinners.
markers: baptism does not count if the pastor is a sinner
a sinful minister's sacraments are invalid
orthodox: The validity of the sacraments rests on Christ's promise, not on the minister's worthiness.

name: Antinomianism
condemned_by: Rejected in the Lutheran Formula of Concord (1577), Westminster Confession (1646) and the New Testament (Rom 6; Jude 4)
teaches: Because we are saved by grace, God's moral law no longer binds believers; obedience and holiness are optional and sin does not matter.
markers: Christians are not required to obey God's commands
since we are under grace, sin does not matter
God does not see the sins of believers so repentance is unnecessary
the law has no place in the Christian life
orthodox: Grace saves and then transforms; the believer pursues holiness as the fruit of faith (Rom 6:1-2; Titus 2:11-12).

name: Judaizing (law-keeping as a requirement for salvation)
condemned_by: Rejected at the Council of Jerusalem (Acts 15) and in Galatians
teaches: Gentile believers must be circumcised or keep the Mosaic law, in addition to faith in Christ, to be saved.
markers: you must keep the Torah to be saved
faith in Jesus is not enough without circumcision or the Sabbath law
orthodox: Salvation is by grace through faith in Christ alone (Gal 2:16; Acts 15).

name: Universal reconciliation (apokatastasis)
condemned_by: Origen's teaching condemned at the Second Council of Constantinople (553); disputed by most traditions today
teaches: Every person, and even the devil, will ultimately be saved regardless of faith in Christ; hell is not final.
markers: everyone will be saved in the end
there is no eternal hell for anyone
all roads lead to heaven
orthodox: Scripture teaches final judgment and salvation through Christ alone (John 14:6; Matt 25:46). Traditions differ on how to state this, so a pastor should decide.

name: Prosperity gospel
condemned_by: Denounced in the Lausanne Movement's Cape Town Commitment (2010) and by many denominations
teaches: God promises believers health and wealth in this life in return for faith or giving; sickness and poverty signal lack of faith.
markers: if you give to this ministry God will multiply it back to you
poverty is a curse and faith will make you rich
if you were truly faithful you would be healed
God wants every believer to be wealthy
orthodox: God cares for his people's needs but promises suffering as well as blessing, and gives himself, not riches, as the reward (Phil 4:11-13; John 16:33).
